title: Theta-window deployment cadence and artifacts index (May 2026) - sketch
content:
Purpose:
This doc is a compact, portable runbook for the new 'theta window' cadence we're trialing for small-feature, low-risk releases. Think of it as the pocket map + artifact index for a 48h micro-deploy with progressive traffic phasing and tight telemetry gates.

Scope and when to use this pattern:
- Small backend changes (router, batching, KV-cache tweaks), model variant swaps, or control-plane feature flips that are low-risk but need observability and discipline.
- Not for schema migrations, big database changes, or infra-level kernel swaps. Use the full cutover playbook in those cases.

High-level flow (theta phases):
1) Prep (T-48 to T-6): documentation, canary images built, smoke branch deployed to staging, rollout calendar published.
2) Alpha (T to T+15m): 0% -> 1% traffic; smoke tests + quick health checks.
3) Beta (T+15m to T+90m): 1% -> 10% traffic; sampling traces, latency baselines.
4) Gamma (T+90m to T+4h): 10% -> 40% traffic; run slow-path load and routing heuristics.
5) Theta (T+4h to T+24h): 40% -> 100% traffic if all gates pass.
6) Afterglow (T+24h to T+48h): stabilize, erode caching pressure, confirm metrics.

Quick checklist (preflight) - owner: release lead
- [ ] Build artifact SHA verified and pushed (CI job: deploy/artifact/2187).
- [ ] Canary config created (linear RD-4123).
- [ ] Observability dashboards copied and annotated (sentry-sampler, traffic-filament view).
- [ ] Rollback image ready and smoke-tested to the same env.
- [ ] Pager duty rotation assigned for the 48h window.
- [ ] Comms message drafted for #deployments and customer-success.

During window - live operators checklist
Alpha (0->1%)
- Confirm service starts cleanly (no crash loops).
- Run quick smoke: generate 10 synthetic requests across common routes.
- Check p50/p95 latency, error-rate, and 5xx counts in the last 5m. Gate: no increase >3x baseline error-rate and p95 within +200ms.

Beta (1->10%)
- Start distributed trace sampling at 20% for canary traffic.
- Verify tail latency (p99) doesn't degrade beyond +400ms in any region.
- Check token-level cost delta on the embedding endpoints (if applicable).
- Gate: no sustained error-rate increase >1% absolute, no new errors with >5 occurrences in 10m.

Gamma (10->40%)
- Run load probes simulating worst-case prompts (long seq, kv-hit/miss).
- Confirm autoscaler behavior: no flapping, CPU/GPU utilization within expected band.
- Validate consecutive request traces for KV cache warmup.
- Gate: CPU/GPU OOMs = 0, tail latency spike < 25% of baseline, no external dependency SLO regressions.

Theta (40->100%)
- Gradual ramp every 30m with small velocity steps (e.g., +10–15%).
- Keep close watch for customer-facing errors and increase debug tracing sampling for correlated requests.
- Gate: sustained telemetry looks healthy for two full sampling windows (30m each).

Afterglow (24–48h)
- Mark the release in the release ledger, add notes to the release channel.
- Schedule a 1h retro with infra, sla, and obs folks if any anomaly was recorded.
- Sweep metrics for any quiet regressions (memory leaks, GC, connection pool exhaustion).

Rollback triggers (explicit)
- Critical: any regression causing total customer API error-rate >2% absolute within 15m.
- Performance: p95 increase >500ms sustained over 30m and correlates to user impact.
- Resource: repeating OOMs or autoscaler inability to provision nodes.
- Unknown errors: new uncategorized 5xx with >20 distinct traces in 10m.

Rollback procedure (fast lane)
- Owner (release lead) announces rollback in #deployments, triggers the prebuilt rollback job (ci/rollback/2187).
- Switch routing back to previous stable variant via the routing service (route-set rollback command).
- Validate rollback success with the same smoke tests used during alpha.
- Post rollback: collect logs and tag the incident with 'theta-rollback' + ticket to triage.

Communication plan
- Preflight: post calendar in #deployments 48h before T with quick links to dashboards and PRs.
- Alpha start: short post in channel: "theta alpha started — 1% — smoke checks in progress".
- Any gate fail: immediate ping to PD owner and @eng-oncall; brief statement: what, when, immediate next action.
- Post success: release note stub in #releases and notify customer-success if any visible behaviour changed.

Staffing timetable (compact) - local times in PDT
- Release Lead (Lindsay Chen): T-48 -> T+4h primary, T+4h -> T+24h fallback
- Observability lead (Rajiv): T-6h -> T+12h (focus on traces and dashboards)
- Platform SRE (Marta): T-2h -> T+8h (autoscaler & infra watch)
- API owner (Ethan): T -> T+6h (owns canary traffic routing)
- Secondary oncall: default PD rotation (see linked artifacts)

Artifact index (where to click)
- CI artifact: github.com/redwood-inference/platform/actions/runs/42187
- Canary config: linear.app/RD/issue/RD-4123-theta-window-canary-config
- Rollback job: github.com/redwood-inference/platform/actions/workflows/rollback-2187.yml
- Dashboard template: confluence.redwood.ai/display/RE/Theta+Window+Playbook#Dashboards
- Release notes stub: confluence.redwood.ai/pages/viewpage.action?pageId=50721

Smoke test matrix (quick litmus):
- route /v1/generate: 12 requests, short prompt, success and response schema match.
- embed endpoints: 8 requests, verify embedding dims and stable cosine on sample vectors.
- streaming path: 6 streaming sessions, ensure disconnect/reconnect path OK.
- long sequence: 4 requests with seq_len > 2k to see memory and tail latency.

Unresolved questions / TO-DOs (notes to self)
- Decide whether theta should enforce a minimum inter-step quiesce period for cross-region warmup (Rajiv).
- Add a simple synthetic user journey that hits both hosted-api and dedicated backends (Ethan).
- Should we gate by cost delta on Optimize signals? Need design doc from product-optimize.

Release notes draft (short) — to be expanded before final release channel post:
Title: "Small routing & KV-cache warmup improvements — phased deployment (theta-window)"
Summary: Ship small optimization to routing and KV-cache warmup that reduces cold-start latency for common prompts and adds better cache eviction heuristics. Rolling deploy using theta-window cadence.
Impacted surfaces: API routing, embedding prewarm, dedicated and hosted routing stacks.
User-facing risks: Minimal. Potential transient latency blips during warmup for long-sequence requests.
Rollout plan: progressive 0->100% over 24h, monitor telemetry, rollback if gate triggers.

If anything goes sideways — remember: keep comms short, name the action (rollback / pause), and use the prebuilt rollback job.

Notes-to-self: this is intentionally compact. If theta sees >3 successful runs without manual intervention, propose we move to product-wide default for small infra flips.

-- Lindsay
